claim: A2: a sintered ceramic tube 17 mm x 106 mm gives 200 mL/min at 10 kPa
law: Radial Darcy flow; ceramic permeability from pot filters (1 to 3 L/h, Akvopedia; 556 L/(m2 h bar) at 15 mm); best case thin 0.2 um layer 10 mL/min

claim: A2: a 0.2 to 1 um ceramic retains cysts and reduces bacteria
law: Size exclusion; pot filters reduce bacteria by about 2 log with silver (Akvopedia)
check: A 1 um rating does not retain 0.3 to 0.5 um bacteria; holds only as reduction, and the option is dropped on X1

claim: A3: copper in the straw inactivates bacteria during a sip
law: Copper pots reduced bacteria over 16 h storage (Sudha et al. 2012); wet copper contact killing takes minutes to hours (Grass et al. 2011)

claim: A3: charcoal removes bacteria and protozoa
law: Granular carbon is an adsorbent, not a size barrier: water passes between 0.4 to 1.7 mm granules
check: Gaps between granules are 100 times a bacterium; carbon can also grow bacteria

claim: A3: copper and charcoal address Cryptosporidium
law: Cryptosporidium oocysts resist chemical disinfectants (chlorine; HWP-CLM-001)

claim: A3: copper released in a sip stays below the 1.3 mg/L action level
law: EPA Lead and Copper Rule action level (Rev A R2)
check: Likely low in a flowing sip; the first draw after wet storage (about 9 dm2 of copper in 17 mL) may exceed it, release rate to assess; not the reason the option fails
